request.docs: Text + image fusion: 'zzqx' appears in no product, which used to filter every result out (all words had to match). With weighted RRF the text only helps ranking, so the image match must still rank in the top 3. Fails with 0 products if the cluster rejected weighted RRF (API log: 'weighted RRF not available').

root.docs: Set collection variable redis_enabled to match REDIS_ENABLED in the API's .env (true / false). Run the folder in order: TC-050 and TC-053 save the ids that later requests reuse.

request.docs: Round-trip PING to Redis. With redis_enabled=false the API reports ok=false and that Redis is disabled.
redis_connected is true when Redis is enabled and reachable, null when disabled.
First text search: the query embedding is stored in Redis and its id returned (saved as query_embedding_id).

items.name: TC-051 Same query again (different case-spaces) returns the same id

request.docs: Same query after normalisation (trim, collapse spaces, lower-case) is served from Redis.

items.name: TC-052 Search by query_embedding_id only (no search_query)

request.docs: Reuses the stored query text and embedding. Redis disabled → 503.
Image embedding and the image (base64) are stored in Redis; the id is saved as image_embedding_id.

items.name: TC-054 Same image again returns the same id

request.docs: Identical image bytes are served from Redis.

items.name: TC-055 Search by image_embedding_id only (no image)

request.docs: Image search using the stored embedding; no upload. Redis disabled → 503.

items.name: TC-056 Text + image by both ids

request.docs: Multimodal search entirely from Redis. Redis disabled → 503.

items.name: TC-057 Unknown or expired embedding id

request.docs: Well-formed id that is not in Redis: 400 when Redis is enabled, 503 when disabled.
Ids must look like asmo:emb:image:<sha256>; rejected without touching Redis (same with Redis on or off).

root.docs: Aligned to ASMO AI Search API Specification v2.0: POST /v1/search (multipart/form-data) and GET /v1/search/suggestions. Response and filter keys are the OpenSearch index field names. Set the category_id variable to a real category id from the index.
